sections.skill: Identify the core parts of a simple written agreement

questions.prompt: Why put an agreement in writing?

choices.text: It replaces the need to do the work
It records what both sides promised
It makes any promise automatically legal everywhere
It hides the price from the customer

questions.correct_answer: It records what both sides promised
questions.intro: A written AGREEMENT (contract) records what both sides promised, so there is less room for "I thought you meant..." A simple service or sales agreement usually covers: who the parties are; what will be delivered (scope); price and payment terms; timeline; what happens if plans change, including cancellation and refunds; who owns the finished work; and how disagreements will be handled. Use plain words, keep a signed copy, and have important or unusual agreements reviewed by an attorney.

sections.skill: A written plan for a group trip

questions.prompt: Why write down the trip plan?

choices.text: Because notes are required by law
So everyone remembers the same thing

questions.correct_answer: So everyone remembers the same thing
questions.intro: Friends planning a trip write down who is coming, where they are going, what it costs, who pays for what, what happens if someone cancels, and how they will decide if they disagree. Without the note, everyone remembers it differently. A business agreement is the written plan for a job, so both sides remember the same thing.
